name: database
description: Deterministic, statement-by-statement transaction engine for teaching database concurrency. Scenarios are tiny tables plus up to three transaction programs (read, locking read, write computed in the application, atomic update, predicate SUM, application check, insert, commit, rollback). A schedule interleaves them, and a concurrency-control engine decides visibility, waiting and aborts: no isolation, locking RU/RC/RR/Serializable (2PL with predicate locks), MVCC Read Committed, snapshot isolation, SSI, InnoDB Repeatable Read, MongoDB snapshot transactions, OCC and a SQLite-style single writer. Anomalies are detected from the history, and a serial-equivalence check runs every order of the same programs.
limits: One statement per tick; a blocked transaction skips its schedule slots and resumes when its lock is free (woken waiters run first).
Rows hold a single integer value and a tag used by predicate queries; at most 3 transactions, 8 statements each, 5 rows, 12 schedule slots, 36 ticks.
Deadlock victim is the transaction whose request closed the cycle (PostgreSQL behaves similarly; InnoDB prefers the smaller transaction).

SSI is modelled as a commit-time check for a cycle in the conflict graph of committed transactions; PostgreSQL detects dangerous structures with predicate (SIREAD) locks and can abort earlier or produce false positives.

InnoDB Repeatable Read: plain reads use a transaction snapshot; UPDATE and locking reads act on the newest committed version; gap/next-key locking for plain UPDATE predicates is not modelled. Serializable is modelled as 2PL with predicate locks.
MongoDB: snapshot reads; any write conflict with an uncommitted or newer committed version aborts immediately (TransientTransactionError).
SQLite: WAL mode with a busy timeout: one writer at a time; a transaction whose snapshot predates a commit gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT when it tries to write.
Profiles reproduce documented visible behaviour for these schedules, not product internals.

dbTrace.description: Per-tick trace rows (0..36) for a scenario index or id under an engine id (none, lock-ru, lock-rc, lock-rr, lock-ser, mvcc-rc, mvcc-si, ssi, innodb-rr, mongo, occ, single). order lists which transaction (1..3) issues its next statement per slot; empty uses the scenario default. retry=1 restarts transactions the database aborted. errors picks product error strings (textbook, postgres, mysql, sqlite, mongodb). Bind with tableBindings.

dbLevelTrace.description: Trace under an isolation level (0 RU, 1 RC, 2 RR, 3 Snapshot, 4 Serializable) as implemented by a profile (0 textbook locking, 1 PostgreSQL, 2 MySQL/InnoDB, 3 SQLite, 4 MongoDB).

dbMechTrace.description: Trace under a mechanism: 0 two-phase locking, 1 OCC, 2 MVCC snapshot isolation, 3 SSI, 4 single writer.

dbEngine.description: Engine id a profile runs for an isolation level.

dbCaption.description: Markdown caption: optional guidance, what happened at this tick, the invariant and anomalies so far.

dbContext.description: Compact factual state for the AI tutor (Scene.promptExpr): transactions, statements, versions, locks, conflict edges, anomalies, serializability, metrics and history.

dbCell.description: Numeric cell of a 2D list (laneCodes, verCodes, lockCodes, edgeCodes); 0 when missing.

dbText.description: Text cell of a 2D list (lanes, verLabels, lockGrid, edgeLabels); empty when missing.

dbAt.description: Item of a list (laneRows, keys); empty when missing.

dbMatrix.description: Isolation matrix code computed by running anomaly scenario row (dirty read, lost update, non-repeatable read, read skew, phantom, write skew) at level col: 0 anomaly, 1 aborted, 2 waited, 3 consistent.

dbMatrixText.description: Short label for an isolation matrix cell.

dbMatrixRow.description: Anomaly name for an isolation matrix row.

dbMechMatrix.description: Mechanism comparison code (scenario row × mechanism col, retries on).

dbMechMatrixText.description: 'ticks · aborts · waits' for a mechanism matrix cell, or ✗ anomaly.

dbMechMatrixRow.description: Scenario name for a mechanism matrix row.

dbOrder.description: Default schedule for a scenario, padded with 0 to 12 slots.

dbOrderText.description: Effective schedule as text, e.g. 'T1 T2 T1'.

dbTxCount.description: Number of transactions in a scenario.

dbProfileNote.description: How the product maps that level, when it differs from the name.

dbSqlLine.description: Active SQL line for a scenario's code file when it is the current scenario; 0 otherwise.

dbOp.description: 1 when an operation kind (read, write, commit, abort, retry, ...) happened this tick.

dbLaneColor.description: Color for a lane code: 0 empty, 1 pending, 2 done, 3 waiting, 4 running, 5 committed, 6 aborted, 7 anomaly.
